```{r}
countydata <- read_csv("county_rel_census.csv") |> clean_names()
metrodata <- read_csv("metro_rel_census.csv") |> clean_names()
statedata <- read_csv("state_rel_census.csv") |> clean_names()
nationdata <- read_csv("nation_rel_census.csv") |> clean_names()
```


##Q1: Which counties that have similar diversity populations have different religious faiths at the top? (For example, does a county in Maryland that has a similar diversity percentage as one in another state near Maryland have the same congregations leading?) 
```{r}
glimpse(countydata)

q1_diversity <- countydata |>
  group_by(state_name, county_name) |>
  summarise(
    total_groups = n()
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(total_groups))

q1_top_rel <- countydata |>
  inner_join(q1_diversity, join_by(state_name, county_name)) 

q1_surroundstates <- q1_top_rel |>
  filter(state_name == "Maryland" |
         state_name == "Virginia" |
         state_name == "Pennsylvania" |
         state_name == "Delaware" |
         state_name == "West Virginia"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(total_groups))

q1_max_adherents <- q1_surroundstates |>
  group_by(state_name, county_name) |>
  summarise( max_adherents = max(adherents, na.rm = TRUE)
)

q1full <- q1_surroundstates |>
  inner_join(q1_max_adherents, join_by(state_name, county_name)) |>
  filter(adherents == max_adherents) |>
  arrange(desc(total_groups))

head(q1full)
```

##Q2: Are there any religious groups dominating at state level that also dominate at county level?
```{r}
q2statetop <- statedata |>
  group_by(state_name) |>
  summarise(
    max_state_adhere = max(adherents, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

q2_staterel <- statedata |>
  inner_join(q2statetop, join_by(state_name)) |>
  filter(adherents == max_state_adhere) |>
  rename(statetopcong = group_name)

q2countytop <- countydata |>
group_by(state_name, county_name) |>
  summarise(max_county_adhere = max(adherents, na.rm = TRUE))

q2_countyrel <-countydata |>
  inner_join(q2countytop, join_by(state_name, county_name)) |>
  filter(adherents == max_county_adhere) |>
  rename(countytopcong = group_name)

q2comparison <-q2_countyrel |>
  inner_join(q2_staterel, join_by(state_name)) |>
  mutate(
    boththesame = countytopcong == statetopcong) |>
  arrange(desc(boththesame))
  
head(q2comparison, 20)
```

##Q3: What are the top few states that have a majority versus the top few states that have a (somewhat equal) balance of congregations based on population of adherents?
```{r}
q3top_staterel <- statedata |>
  group_by(state_name) |>
  summarise(
    total_adherents = sum(adherents, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) 

##grouping census data by state and shows total number of adherent sin each state
  
state_pop <- get_acs(geography = "state",
              variables = c(population = "B01001_001"),
              year = 2021,
              geometry = TRUE)
##pop data from all states, the variable is the total pop (API key?)

state_pop_with_religion <- state_pop |>
  left_join(q3top_staterel, join_by(NAME == state_name)) 

q3top_staterel <- q3top_staterel |>
  mutate(rate = total_adherents)

q3people_to_rel <- statedata |>
  inner_join(q3top_staterel, join_by(state_name))

q3people_to_rel <- q3people_to_rel |>
  mutate(religion_pct = adherents/total_adherents)

q3majority <- q3people_to_rel |>
  group_by(state_name) |>
  summarise(
    largest = max(religion_pct, na.rm = TRUE) 
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(largest))

q3minority <- tail(q3majority, 10)

glimpse(q3majority)
glimpse(q3minority)
```

##Q4: Are there specific “pockets” of congregations across the state? (Mapping clusters of congregations) - since I don't have any zip data, I wasn't able to find any clusters of different congregations. I ended up going with the magma chart. 

```{r}
md_counties <- countydata |>
  filter(str_detect(state_name, "Maryland"))
##this is just filtering the state to be specifically Maryland. now, i want to see where a few of the big congregations are clustered around the state

q4_pockets <- md_counties |>
  group_by(fips) |>
  summarise(
    total_congregations = sum(congregations, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
arrange(desc(total_congregations))


md_all <- counties(
  state = "Maryland",
  year = 2021)

md_map_religion_all <- md_all |>
  left_join(q4_pockets, join_by(GEOID == fips)) 


ggplot(md_map_religion_all) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill=total_congregations)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_b(option="magma", trans = "log") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title="Overall Pocket Data of MD Congregations",
       fill="Congregations")

```

##Q5:Which groups have the highest total adherent populations compared to their number of congregations?
```{r}
q5adherepercong <- statedata |>
  group_by(group_name) |>
  summarise(
    total_adherents = sum(adherents, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_congregations = sum(congregations, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    adherents_per_cong = total_adherents / total_congregations
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(adherents_per_cong))

head(q5adherepercong, 20)

##This question/code was the simplest because for the longest time I didn't know what I wanted as my fifth question, but I was interested in seeing which groups had the most adherents compared to how many congregations they also had. I think it would be interesting to see in a journalist's sense which states these groups dominate in and why? Is it because of history, people who have moved there, etc.
```
